meta.title: Atlas of the Silence
author_notes: The Last Dawn's return lies roughly 400 years after the 1487-1488 AS events (c. 1900 AS). No page states this; in-world nobody knows when. No 1488 AS figure (Mihail, Elric, etc.) is the Last Dawn.
Direction: when the Ustrus creditors come to Ocristan, Mihail plays for time. He pays a little, stalls, and keeps all three empires guessing; nothing settles in 1488 AS.
Bloria grown in run 2 (Aldrecht, Hollmar, blood-seals). Canvas grown to x -300..1100, y -300..900 after run 2; Kalderhof now sits well north of Aldrecht.
Tamarun's unmarked name in the Margin is not a death mark: the hand is deciding whether to use him. He stays emperor for now. No page says this.
The old Rookery brother who struck a bill stays unconfirmed as Kaspar Hollmar on every page.
Next run: grow western Veleh (Tullanon, the Olta, Trantar's villages, why the Hundred-Eleven recruits there).

calendar.year_zero: The Silence: the disappearance of the kimberstone builders
calendar.notes: Years only for now; no named months yet. The 111 journal's Day 1 falls in 1487 AS; its Day 438 falls in 1488 AS. Winter's worst stretch is called 'the long night' in Veleh; Ustrus has a rainy season instead of snow.

realms.name: Veleh
realms.summary: Fractured kingdom in the seam between three empires. Capital Ocristan. Ustrus has held it by proxy for about fifty years.

realms.name: Bloria
realms.summary: Northwestern empire, capital Aldrecht. Bankrolls Baron Mihail as a proxy against Ustrus. One of the Thirteen rules behind it: the Lady of the Ledger, by common belief.

realms.name: Mechil
realms.summary: Northeastern empire. Has not moved on Veleh in about a hundred years. One of the Thirteen rules behind it.

realms.name: Ustrus
realms.summary: Southeastern empire, capital Beit Haifud. Overlord-by-proxy of Veleh. One of the Thirteen rules behind it.

places.name: Tullanon
places.summary: Swamp city on rotting pillars over the Olta. Clams, fog, slums. Where the Hundred-Eleven recruited Alden.

places.name: The Rift
places.summary: White kimberstone fortress at the meeting of the Olta and Krisen. Seven towers, one broken. Fell in 1487 AS.

places.name: Ocristan
places.summary: Walled capital of Veleh, seat of the council. Bought with Ustrus gold in 1487 AS.

places.name: Trantar
places.summary: Bone-walled city on Veleh's western border. Where the peasant revolt broke in 1488 AS.

places.name: Vorn Danu crossing
places.summary: The great river dividing Veleh from Ustrus. Its main crossing stands on kimberstone legs.

places.name: The Blackmire
places.summary: Fen south of the Rift between the Krisen, Olta and Vorn Danu. Home of the witch-line that sells years and takes payment in other lives.

places.name: Haldevin
places.summary: Mill village in the western foothills. Raised men for the Trantar rising under Dean Farrick's squad; burned by the tax riders in 1488 AS, its church register taken.

places.name: Crow's Pass
places.summary: High saddle on the Bloria border under a freestanding kimberstone arch. Mihail died and was raised on its sill in 1472 AS; his household has held it since.

places.name: Kalderhof
places.summary: Walled crown estate on the northern moors of Bloria where the Ostvald lower bond ends. Named by everyone, visited by no one. Said to spend debtors a year at a time; sends out only ash.

places.name: Aldrecht
places.summary: Walled crown city of Bloria at the springs of the Olta. The Burg, the Ostvald exchange, the great Bond. Twice besieged by Ustrus, never taken. Seat of the old king Eberwin III.

places.name: The Rookery
places.summary: Monastery of a mute order in the north-eastern forest, a day from the Mechil border, ringed by a vast crow roost. Untaxed, untouched by Mechil. Where Mihail met Mechil's envoys in 1488 AS. Held in the north-east to be where Mechil listens to the crows.

places.name: Vadra
places.summary: Lordless fishing town on the Strova coast, run by a compact of boat-owners called the Benches. Landed the Ustrus gold in 1487 AS; buried the galley dead that washed up after, and kept eleven Counting-House tallies cut from their collars.

people.name: Baron Mihail
people.summary: Revenant baron bidding for the throne of Veleh, caught between three empires.

people.name: Lord Andrej
people.summary: Last lord of the Rift. Held it five weeks against Mihail's larger army; lost it when the Hundred-Eleven opened the gate from inside. Died caged in the sun, 1487 AS. His children are Mihail's wards.

people.name: Aran
people.summary: Mage sent by an unremembered empire to break the Rift for an army. Burned his soul to snap the seventh tower; the army never came. The top of the tower lies in the Krisen.

people.name: Tamarun
people.summary: The young Emperor of Ustrus. Went around his own Counting-House to lend Mihail gold, apparently to turn Veleh against Bloria. Whether he knows what stands behind his throne is unconfirmed.

people.name: Edrun Vasselt
people.summary: Bloria's factor in Ocristan; pays Mihail in blood-sealed bills. Bought a copy of the Ustrus loan terms and sold his silence to Mihail instead of sending it home.

people.name: Wendel Raust
people.summary: Ostvald reckoner, the gray rider. Audited Edrun Vasselt's books in Ocristan over the winter of 1487 AS and offered the Hundred-Eleven a second contract with the houses. Elric refused; Raust left by the west gate.

people.name: Ilinca
people.summary: Lord Andrej's daughter, about twelve in 1488 AS. With her brother Vasko, the Rift's legal heir, a ward in Baron Mihail's household since the fall. Said to have her nurse's mind-witch gift.

people.name: Grigore Tal
people.summary: Castellan of the Rift since 1487 AS, holding it for the boy Vasko under Mihail's wardship. One of the men who carried Mihail off the field at Crow's Pass; sixteen years in its garrison. Will not speak of the arch or stand in a gateway.

people.name: Kaspar Hollmar
people.summary: Head of House Hollmar, ruined c. 1458 AS; named the Lady aloud at court and fled. By report a mute brother of the Rookery since. Said to know how to strike a name from the crown's book from the bill's end; a bill rotted under his thumbnail at the Mechil embassy.

people.name: Elric
people.summary: Centurion, Number One of the Hundred-Eleven. Crossed the Eastern Sea c. 1424 AS.

people.name: Olegzander
people.summary: Ustrus's proxy, king of Veleh 1485–1487 AS. Called the Putrid for a Blackmire rot that never killed him. Brought down by a false story that he sold the Rift; dead in 1487 AS.

lore.name: The Thirteen
lore.summary: Thirteen nigh-immortals who rule through empires and war on each other. Prophesied to fall to the Last Dawn.

lore.name: The Grimoire
lore.summary: Book bound in human skin. Binds the 111 men of the Hundred-Eleven. A will of its own.

lore.name: Kimberstone
lore.summary: The builders' white stone. Proof against every tool and siege engine; only rare, costly magic has ever broken it. Hidden under old Tullanon as well as standing at the Rift.

lore.name: The Counting-House
lore.summary: Ustrus's revenue office in Beit Haifud. Taxes Veleh in goods and in people. Answers to the power behind the Ustrus throne, not the Emperor.

lore.name: The Last Dawn
lore.summary: A single old fragment says the Last Dawn will return and end the Thirteen. Copies disagree on every key word. No power openly hunts it; tax riders put out its candles.

lore.name: The Ostvald Houses
lore.summary: Bloria's banking families. Lend to crown and lords on terms that cannot be met, take people in bond, seal their bills in debtors' blood. Long-held debtors go north by night and do not return.

lore.name: The Lady of the Ledger
lore.summary: Bloria's one of the Thirteen, as Blorians name it: a woman of middle years who has held the crown's book of debts at every coronation in the rolls, under a new name and office each reign. In 1488 AS taken to be Lady Hedwen, Mistress of the Privy Roll.

lore.name: Blood-Seals
lore.summary: The red seals on Ostvald bills, mixed with a bonded debtor's blood. By reckoners' teaching a seal holds only while its debtor's name stands in the crown's book; a struck name rots it, a dead one turns it to powder. The debtor feels where his bill lies.

lore.name: Bound Relics
lore.summary: Objects with a will that bind a company of men, each by a different count, gift and price: the Grimoire, the Drum, the Chain, the Grey Standard. By the custom called the Courtesy, no two bound companies have ever met in the field.

lore.name: The Margin
lore.summary: The Counting-House has no head. Its orders appear overnight, unsigned, in the margins of the second ledger, in an old hand nobody in the building owns. Known chiefly from a runaway clerk, 1488 AS.

events.name: The Silence
events.summary: The kimberstone builders vanish. Year zero of the common reckoning.

events.name: The Rift's last capture before 1487
events.summary: After this the Rift is said to be untakeable. By whom it was taken is not recorded.

events.name: Breaking of the Bridge
events.summary: A beaten army retreating north breaks the builders' Vorn Danu bridge behind it; its mages spend the whole town of Ostrel to do it. The river at the crossing goes still one night a year since.

events.name: Aran breaks the seventh tower
events.summary: A mage burns his soul to snap one of the Rift's towers for an army that never comes. Before the capture of c. 1187; date otherwise disputed.

events.name: First siege of Aldrecht
events.summary: An Ustrus army besieges the Blorian capital and breaks camp in autumn with the walls unbreached.

events.name: Second siege of Aldrecht
events.summary: Two months; the inner wall undermined in three places. A relief army paid on Ostvald bills breaks the Ustrus camp a day before the city falls.

events.name: The Hollmar Failure
events.summary: House Hollmar accepts a loan repaid in full and frees four hundred bonded tenants. Its seals rot within a season; the other houses buy its debts and the family goes into bond. Its head, Kaspar Hollmar, names the Lady aloud at court and flees.

events.name: Eberwin III crowned in Aldrecht
events.summary: Lady Hedwen holds the book in the closed room. She is said not to have changed since.

events.name: Mechil's last march into Veleh
events.summary: A Mechil army comes south through the north-eastern forest, burns two villages and passes the Rookery by. Mechil has not moved on Veleh since.

events.name: Elric crosses the Eastern Sea
events.summary: Elric arrives from the uncharted east, twenty-one days at sea, tied to the mast.

events.name: Ustrus takes Veleh by proxy
events.summary: Ustrus begins taxing Veleh through proxy politicians.

events.name: Battle of Crow's Pass
events.summary: Mihail dies with three arrows in the chest, and comes back.

events.name: Death of the last king of Veleh
events.summary: Arrow through the throat; some say murder. A dozen barons raise levies.

events.name: Olegzander crowned
events.summary: The council, at Ustrus's word, crowns the voievod who runs its tax press. Rival barons are paid to disband.

events.name: Fall of the Rift
events.summary: Mihail and the Hundred-Eleven take the fortress that could not fall.

events.name: Fall of King Olegzander
events.summary: A story that he sold the Rift, written by Mihail's household before the siege, costs him the crown. After the bought vote the Hundred-Eleven kill him near the west gate on Mihail's order; no body shown.

events.name: The Gold Run
events.summary: Mihail's journey to Beit Haifud and back with an Ustrus loan in gold. Hunted by bloodhounds and galleys sent from inside Ustrus.

events.name: Burning of Haldevin
events.summary: After Trantar the tax riders return with soldiers, burn the village and take its church register.

events.name: The Mechil Embassy
events.summary: While Trantar burns, Mihail rides east in secret and offers to default on the Ustrus loan if Mechil will stand behind him. The envoys listen and give no answer.

events.name: The Drowned Clerk
events.summary: Iacob Serdan, the chancery clerk who sold Vasselt a copy of the Ustrus loan terms, is found in Ocristan's town ditch. Self-drowned, by the wardens' finding; his note says he sold the terms twice.
